reason: Correction of an earlier flawed comparison that conflated tree+building shade with tree-alone shade, attributing the whole ambient-vs-combined difference to trees. Buildings are an existing urban condition, not a planting intervention -- their baseline effect must be isolated.

method.tree_shade_coefficient_source: thermal.era5_utci.DEFAULT_UTCI_REDUCTION_FULL_SHADE_C -- canopy-specific literature range, already documented in that module
method.building_shade_coefficient: NOT calibrated -- no literature-backed UTCI-specific building-shade constant exists in this codebase. Primary decomposition table uses building_coef=tree_coef (ratio=1.0) as one point on an explicit sensitivity grid (0.25/0.50/0.75/1.00 x tree_coef), never presented as a calibrated value.
method.BT_combination_rule: marginal-weighted: tree-only-area*tree_coef + building-only-area*building_coef + overlap-area*max(tree_coef,building_coef) -- documented modelling choice (a point cannot be cooled by more than the stronger of two overlapping shadows), not a measured fact.
method.building_daylight_gating: hard cutoff at solar_elevation<=0 (baked into building_shadow_fraction at the ray-casting stage)
method.gating_note: these two gating mechanisms are NOT normalized against each other -- documented as a real, unresolved modelling asymmetry, not something this analysis corrects.

corrected_claims.allowed: Including urban morphology substantially changes the estimated total radiative-shade burden, particularly under winter conditions.
corrected_claims.to_verify_not_yet_asserted: The marginal thermal value of tree canopy changes when existing building shade is included (sensitivity grid shows this marginal value is in fact fairly STABLE across building-coefficient ratios 0.25-1.00x -- e.g. 2022-07-14 tree_heat_benefit_given_buildings varies only ~331k-336k, a ~1.4% range -- so this claim is plausible but the building coefficient itself remains uncalibrated).
corrected_claims.forbidden_and_not_made: "Buildings increase the winter cost of trees by 13-15x" -- decomposition shows the 2022-02-08 combined_cold_cost (216,222) is ~93% building baseline (201,613) and only ~7% (14,609) is the tree's own marginal cost given buildings; the deciduous case (leaf-cover=0) confirms this exactly: combined_cold_cost (201,613) equals building_cold_cost to the last digit.

mandatory_tests_status.deciduous_leaf_cover_0_T_approx_0_vs_0: PASS (test_deciduous_zero_leaf_cover_T_equals_zero; confirmed on real data: tree_cold_cost_open=0.0, tree_heat_benefit_open=0.0 for all deciduous winter rows)
mandatory_tests_status.deciduous_leaf_cover_0_BT_approx_B: PASS (test_deciduous_zero_leaf_cover_BT_equals_B; confirmed on real data: combined_cold_cost == building_cold_cost exactly for deciduous, e.g. 201612.636212 == 201612.636212)
mandatory_tests_status.no_nan_inf: PASS (verified on real decomposition table, see palma_pilot_four_state_decomposition.csv)
mandatory_tests_status.reproducibility: deterministic, no randomness in the analysis pipeline itself (only in unit-test fixtures)
mandatory_tests_status.building_shadow_geometric_checks: covered by existing tests/unit/test_building_shadow.py (azimuth convention, ray direction toward sun, NoData handling, [0,1] bounds, night=0, isolated-building analytic boundary, azimuth flip) -- not re-run here, no code change to building_shadow.py
